claims.claim: Under the Day 1 pass criteria as revised before any evaluation (chord_sr > 0, maniptrans_sr > 0 and ADD-AUC above the static-object baseline), neither final policy passes.
Under the original Day 1 pass criteria (ADD-AUC > 0.465 instead of the static baseline), neither final policy passes either.
Both final policies satisfy chord_sr > 0 and maniptrans_sr > 0 and fail only the ADD-AUC criterion.
On ADD-AUC and on mean object position error, both final policies do worse than an object that is never moved.
The ml40 policy's mean object orientation error is only about 7 degrees lower than that of a never-moving object, so it reproduces little of the reference rotation.
In this single-seed comparison on one sequence, the run with the 10M replay buffer outperformed the run with the 1M buffer on task-native success rate (chord_sr), mean object position error and MPPE.
The training-curve gap between the 1M-buffer and the 10M-buffer runs is already present in curriculum stage 0, while the virtual object controller scale is still 1.
In both runs the object orientation tracking error during training rises as the virtual object controller scale is decayed to zero.

The chord_sr in the evaluation output is the task-native reference-tracking success rate with pelvis, palm and object limits, and the termination_cause_fraction field comes from a different, legacy object-centric scorer.
In the 9/25 smoke evaluation every world crossed the task-native object, palm and pelvis limits.
The inputs used to evaluate the mf4090 policy on ml40 were byte-identical to those on mf4090.
The static-object baseline was computed with the evaluator's own reference loader and metric functions, reading the reference parquet named in the evaluated policy's embedded config.
Both Day 1 runs trained on the same ep20 reference parquet, with an identical sha256 on both machines.
The ml40 final policy was evaluated with 4096 worlds.
The mf4090 final policy achieved a higher task-native success rate (chord_sr) than the ml40 final policy.
